businessContext: Client: Martin / U-Proof, a South African manufacturer and provider of specialized waterproofing, sealants, and building products.
Creative Touch mandate: Rebuild and audit the WooCommerce ecommerce site after a prior developer relationship ended without handover; improve the existing design without redesigning from scratch.
Target custom domain: uproof.co.za (currently not DNS-connected; live development sits on hostinger staging teal-sparrow-432062.hostingersite.com).
Pricing model: Specific client-supplied retail pricing including VAT for Liquid Rubber, Fibre Filler, Wall & Roof Paint, Zinc Phosphate Primer, Bonding Liquid Primer, Plaster Primer, and Membranes.

Fulfillment & Payments: Client requires live courier integration (Fastway Couriers) over flat rates, and online payment options (Payflex BNPL and credit card gateways) to avoid reliance on manual EFT.
existingSiteFindings: Domain & DNS: The primary custom domain uproof.co.za is not yet pointed via DNS; current live site operates under https://teal-sparrow-432062.hostingersite.com/.
Catalog display issues: The /shop page shows 5 category tabs, but only one single product ('Liquid Rubber' at R790) is rendered on the page.

Homepage pricing and featured products: Featured cards for Bonding Liquid Primer (5L & 20L) display no price, while Fibre Filler 20L displays R500,00—conflicting directly with the client's master retail price list of R1590,00.

Address discrepancy: The live Contact page specifies 'Shop 5, Vision 21 Industrial Park, Steel Road, Duncanville, Vereeniging, 1929', whereas Creative Touch's 2026-09-02 audit recorded and set WooCommerce shipping origin to 'Unit 4, Gateway Industrial Park, 12 Grader Road, Sebenza, Edenvale, Johannesburg, 1609'.
Contact information: Includes a valid-format primary phone (+27 11 450 1234) alongside a placeholder number (+27100000000) in the header.
Navigation and Links: Multiple homepage Application 'Read more' links and featured product actions use placeholder fragment anchors ('#').

Page Builder & Technical Stack: Product metadata reveals 'Elementor 4.2.4', whereas prior audit recorded 10Web WVC builder engine; non-JS fetches returned empty body tags for product detail URLs, requiring headless/browser DOM verification.
Blog & Teasers: Homepage features placeholder articles with future publication dates (June 26, 2026) and admin author handle 'ctsa-admin'.
competitorInsights: No competitor research was performed in this research pass.
risks: Customer confusion and checkout errors resulting from conflicting business address details between the Contact page (Vereeniging) and WooCommerce store settings (Edenvale).
Financial loss or sales loss from display of incorrect pricing (e.g., Fibre Filler 20L listed at R500 instead of R1590) or unpriced product cards.
Reduced online conversions due to incomplete catalog rendering on the main Shop page where only 1 product displays out of 5 categories.
Potential trust erosion caused by placeholder telephone numbers (+27100000000), future-dated blog posts, and non-functional '#' links.
Checkout failures if payment gateways (Paystack/Payflex) and live shipping methods (Fastway) are not configured with active live credentials prior to domain cutover.
recommendations: Reconcile physical business address with client (Vereeniging vs. Edenvale) and align both WooCommerce shipping origin settings and Contact page content.
Correct catalog query/display settings in WooCommerce so that all product categories, variations, and correct prices (matching the master price list) display on /shop and homepage.
Update featured product cards to link to real product URLs and display validated pricing (fix Fibre Filler 20L to R1590).
Remove placeholder phone number (+27100000000) and replace or hide placeholder blog posts/authors prior to launch.
Complete live credentialing and API configuration for Paystack, Payflex, and Fastway Couriers shipping integration.
Perform full rendered browser/visual testing on WooCommerce product detail pages to verify Elementor template rendering.
Execute official DNS migration connecting uproof.co.za once staging audit and human QA sign-off are completed.

seoArchitecture: Primary keyword focus by page type: Home targets brand + category head terms ('waterproofing products South Africa', 'U-Proof waterproofing'); Shop and category pages target transactional terms ('buy liquid rubber waterproofing 5L/20L', 'fibre filler crack repair price', 'waterproofing membrane South Africa'); Help & Advice articles target informational long-tail terms ('how to apply liquid rubber', 'surface preparation before waterproofing', 'waterproofing FAQ South Africa').

Category-page architecture: /shop acts as the top-level catalog hub linking into 5 real category pages (Liquid Rubber, Fibre Filler, Wall & Roof Paint, Primers, Membrane) so each category can independently rank for its own product-plus-size search terms rather than competing against a single flattened shop page.

Solution/application layer (/waterproofing-solutions, /applications) sits between Home and Shop to capture problem-led search intent ('leaking roof solution', 'how to seal a cracked wall') and funnel it into the correct product category, supporting the Problem-Led Application Journey from the site blueprint.

Help & Advice hub structured as a genuine content cluster (not placeholder teasers) with 3 real articles interlinked in a logical sequence (prepare -> apply -> troubleshoot/FAQ), each carrying inline links into the product categories they reference, to build topical authority and support long-tail informational rankings.

Metadata discipline: every page title and meta description reflects only verified real pricing and real page states from PROJECT FACTS and the research report - no invented prices, no claims that unresolved technical issues (e.g. shop catalog rendering, address/shipping-origin mismatch) are already fixed.

Trust and local-SEO signals (verified phone +27 11 450 1234, business address once reconciled, Fastway/Paystack/Payflex badges) surfaced consistently across Home, Shop, category and Contact pages to support both conversion and local business search signals once the address discrepancy is resolved by the client.

Internal linking is structured hub-and-spoke: Home and Shop are hubs; category pages, application anchors and Help & Advice articles are spokes that link back to their hub and sideways to closely related spokes, avoiding orphaned pages.

pages.title: Surface Preparation Guide for Waterproofing | U-Proof Help & Advice
pages.metaDescription: A real, practical guide to preparing roofs, walls and concrete surfaces before waterproofing - cleaning, repairing, priming and moisture-checking, from U-Proof.
pages.h1: How to Prepare a Surface Before Waterproofing
sections: Why surface preparation matters: adhesion failure is the leading cause of waterproofing system failure, more than product quality itself.
Step 1 - Clean: remove dust, loose paint, algae and grease; guidance on pressure-washing and drying times before proceeding.
Step 2 - Repair: fill cracks and holes with Fibre Filler before priming, with a direct link to /product-category/fibre-filler.

Step 3 - Prime: choose the correct primer for the substrate - Zinc Phosphate Primer for metal roofing, Bonding Liquid Primer for smooth/dense surfaces, Plaster Primer for new plaster - linking to /product-category/primers.
Step 4 - Moisture check: how to confirm a surface is dry enough to proceed, including a simple plastic-sheet moisture test contractors can do on site.
Step 5 - Reinforce: where to add Membrane over joints and cracks before the topcoat, linking to /product-category/membrane.
Next step callout linking forward to 'How to Apply Liquid Rubber' as the natural continuation of this guide.

pages.h1: How to Apply Liquid Rubber the Right Way
sections: Before you start: confirm the surface has been prepared per the Surface Preparation Guide (linked), and check ambient temperature and weather forecast (avoid application before rain).
Tools needed: brush, roller or squeegee, mixing paddle, and Membrane strips for joints and cracks (linked to /product-category/membrane).

Step-by-step application: first coat, embedding membrane into a wet first coat over joints/cracks, second coat once tack-free, recommended coverage rate per litre based on container size (5L vs 20L, linked to /product-category/liquid-rubber for sizing/pricing).
Drying and curing times between coats and before the surface is exposed to foot traffic or rain.
Common mistakes to avoid: applying too thin a coat, skipping primer on porous or metal substrates, applying in direct midday heat.
Maintenance tips: periodic inspection and recoating schedule for roofs versus walls.
Related reading link to FAQs for troubleshooting questions like bubbling, poor adhesion or colour fading.

risks: This is a read-only planning pass: Agent 05 holds no site credentials, WP-CLI/SSH, or execution tools in this run. Nothing in this build_plan has been built, previewed, or published - it is a proposal for human-supervised execution only.

Prior audit (2026-09-02) found no shipping zones/methods configured and a silent no-shipping checkout; this build_plan deliberately excludes any shipping configuration (RED-tier - carrier account/credentials) and flags it as an unresolved open question rather than a completed fix.

Fastway Couriers live-rate integration referenced throughout site_blueprint/content_pack as the intended checkout experience has no confirmed credentials or account setup as of last audit; until resolved, checkout cannot actually deliver live courier rates regardless of any front-end badge/copy work done in these tickets.

Paystack and Payflex were installed but never configured with real credentials per prior audit; this build_plan does not configure payment gateways (RED-tier) and any 'Trust & Payment Badge' components built under these tickets must not be interpreted as evidence that payments are live.

Only BACS/Cheque/COD are currently enabled as payment methods per prior audit; if this has not changed, the site's actual checkout path diverges materially from the Payflex/Paystack-first conversion logic in site_blueprint, and front-end badge work could mislead customers if published before gateways are truly configured.

A third-party 10Web trial domain (allowed-pony.10web.cloud) was found hardcoded into compiled Shop/Product/Cart/Checkout build files for logo/breadcrumb/footer/payment-icon assets as of 2026-09-02; it was stripped from on-disk files in a housekeeping pass but not independently re-verified live since - any Elementor rebuild in this plan must re-check for and eliminate this dependency, and its current live status is unconfirmed.

WooCommerce shipping-origin address reconciliation with the Contact page address (Unit 4, Gateway Industrial Park, Sebenza, Edenvale, Johannesburg) was corrected as of the last audit but has not been re-verified fresh; address drift could silently break any future live shipping-rate calculation.

Order-notification emails were found going to Creative Touch's own address rather than the client's business inbox, and the outgoing from-address used a leftover third-party domain; both were flagged but not resolved in the prior audit and are not addressed by this build_plan (outside Agent 05's WordPress/Elementor/WooCommerce catalog scope as defined here).

content_pack v1 itself flags that only one product category was confirmed rendering live in research on /shop, and explicitly states this must be verified fresh before publishing any claim that the 5-category catalog is fixed; the Shop-Catalog Query Fix ticket addresses the intended fix but its actual live effect must be QA-verified before any launch claim is made.

Bespoke SEO copy for Fibre Filler, Wall & Roof Paint, and Primers category pages was not supplied in content_pack v1 (only Liquid Rubber and Membrane had dedicated copy); the corresponding ticket builds template-parity pages using only site_blueprint/PROJECT FACTS data and flags the copy gap rather than inventing content.

A placeholder-style phone number pattern (+27100000000) was noted in prior audit; this build_plan assumes it is still present and schedules its removal, but this has not been freshly re-verified as still live.

No actual visual renders, screenshots, or brand color files were supplied to the design_system stage - the palette/typography tokens in this plan are a proposed hypothesis requiring human designer sign-off against the live/staging visual state before implementation proceeds past PREVIEW.
All AMBER-tier tickets in this plan require explicit human approval before any execution step is taken, per doctrine; none of the structural/template changes described here may be auto-applied.

inputArtifacts.title: U-Proof QA Report (Stage 6)
inputArtifacts.summary: Reviewed research_report v1, site_blueprint v1, design_system v1, content_pack v1, and build_plan v1 as an independent auditor. Overall the artifacts are reasonably disciplined about not claiming unverified live fixes, and content_pack in particular is commendably explicit about the shop-catalog caveat. However, several concrete defects were found: (1) content_pack's page-by-page section descriptions (e.g. Home page "no unpriced or '#' cards", full 5-category tiles) read as accomplished fact in the per-page body even though the summary caveats only the /shop page explicitly - this is an internal inconsistency between the artifact's own summary discipline and its page-level copy, which could be misread as claiming fixes beyond what was verified. (2) build_plan's visible ticket list (only partially available due to truncation) does not yet show explicit tickets for several research_report-flagged issues: the address/contact-page vs WooCommerce shipping-origin mismatch (Vereeniging vs Edenvale), the future-dated/fake-author blog placeholder cleanup beyond the 3 Help & Advice articles, the order-notification email misconfiguration (going to Creative Touch instead of client, and leftover third-party from-address) noted in PROJECT FACTS, the 10Web trial-domain asset hardcoding re-verification, and the Elementor-vs-10Web builder engine discrepancy noted in research - none of these appear as their own tickets in the visible portion of build_plan, and it is not certain from the truncated artifact that they exist further down; this must be confirmed with the human reviewer rather than assumed dropped. (3) design_system's vision-limitation disclaimer is honestly stated and is correctly not overridden by build_plan, which explicitly scopes AMBER-gated ticket work without claiming visual fidelity to any real live screenshots - this is consistent and is not a defect, but is flagged as an area requiring explicit human visual sign-off before CONTROLLED ACTIVATION TESTING. (4) No invented prices, pages, or credentials were found; all pricing in site_blueprint, design_system references, and content_pack traces cleanly to PROJECT FACTS. (5) content_pack and build_plan both correctly keep RED-tier items (DNS, payment credentials, shipping) out of scope, consistent with doctrine. (6) research_report itself surfaces a new/unresolved technical claim (Elementor 4.2.4 vs prior-recorded 10Web WVC builder) that is acknowledged but not turned into any follow-up verification ticket in the visible build_plan - this is a coverage gap. Given the ticket-coverage gaps and the Home-page-copy overconfidence inconsistency, this pass is not clean; it surfaces real planning-artifact defects that need author revision and human review before this moves further down the pipeline. QA is not yet at zero P0/P1, so per doctrine this does not clear the artifacts for advancement without correction.

knowledge.title: Every build passes through the safety pipeline
knowledge.content: BUILD -> PREVIEW -> HUMAN DESIGN APPROVAL -> QA -> FINAL REGRESSION AUDIT -> CONTROLLED ACTIVATION TESTING -> HUMAN LAUNCH APPROVAL -> LIVE. No stage may be skipped by an agent.

knowledge.title: GREEN / AMBER / RED permission tiers
knowledge.content: GREEN actions run automatically. AMBER actions require explicit human approval before execution. RED actions (DNS, registrar, payment credentials, destructive infrastructure) are never executed by an agent without explicit, named authorization.

knowledge.title: Launch never auto-approves
knowledge.content: QA at zero is necessary, never sufficient, for launch. Launch requires human approval; approving with open launch holds is a deliberate, recorded human decision.

knowledge.title: Agents propose; humans approve knowledge
knowledge.content: Agents may propose lesson candidates. No agent may promote its own output into AGENCY or DOCTRINE knowledge. Human approval is the only path from CANDIDATE to APPROVED.

knowledge.title: U-Proof business context
knowledge.content: The client (Martin) owns a South African waterproofing/building-products company, U-Proof. Creative Touch is rebuilding/completing the company's ecommerce website on WordPress + WooCommerce after a prior developer relationship broke down without a proper handover. The client likes the existing design and wants it completed and improved, not redesigned. The client does not want manual/flat-rate shipping and prefers live courier rates (Fastway Couriers); Payflex (SA buy-now-pay-later) was under evaluation alongside a standard card gateway, because the client does not want EFT/manual payment as the primary path.
